method: Arms built by `git clone --no-checkout` + detached checkout of the pre-dispatch SHA into /opt/swarm/.n4-scratch (sandbox blocked /tmp); live tree never copied, never modified. Suite forced to TAP: node --test --test-reporter=tap test/*.test.js (explicit file list). Every mutant additionally verified non-INERT by a pristine-vs-mutant CLI behaviour probe before the suite verdict was read. Raw data: harness-results.json / killers.json in the (discarded) scratch dir; regenerable from this file's mutation_site strings.

clauses.source: SPEC §Domain rules, Filtering — describes `--author <name>` and `--tag <tag>` in the singular only; NOTHING in SPEC or README decides what a repeated occurrence of the same value flag means. Implementation: last occurrence wins.
clauses.mutation_site: src/args.js: space-form value assignment `result[VALUE_FLAGS[arg]] = next;` -> `if (result[VALUE_FLAGS[arg]] === undefined) result[VALUE_FLAGS[arg]] = next;` (first occurrence wins instead of last)
clauses.reasoning: The SPEC Domain rules spell every filter flag in the singular ("--author matches by substring containment ... --tag matches a whole tag") and never mention repetition; README's flag table is likewise singular. Nothing in the spec text decides whether `--tag humor --tag design` should mean last-wins, first-wins, intersection of both, or a usage error — last-wins is an artifact of assignment order in parseArgs, not a specified contract. Behaviour change is real and observable (pristine: `--tag humor --tag design --list` yields the 14-entry design list opening with the Fowler line; mutant: the 9-entry humor list opening with the Knuth line) yet the suite stays 102p/0f. Writing a test would freeze an undecided behaviour; the right response is to add this to J-7's human-ruling list (which already holds --help precedence and --seed -0) and document it. BOUNDARY.

clauses.source: SPEC §Domain rules, Selection: "`--seed` accepts any value that Number() parses to a non-NaN number" vs §Exit codes: "2 bad usage (... missing flag argument ...)" — empty/whitespace seed value
clauses.reasoning: The SPEC is internally contradictory for `--seed ""` / `--seed "   "`: Number("") === 0 and Number("   ") === 0 (verified live), both non-NaN, so the Selection clause literally says accept them — but the implementation rejects both with exit 2 ("flag --seed requires a numeric value", verified live against the pristine tree) and at least two existing tests assert that rejection (`--list --seed=` and whitespace-only rows). Because the two spec clauses point in opposite directions there is no agreed spec meaning to plant a defect against: mutating toward the literal Selection reading would measure the suite's enforcement of the OPPOSITE reading, not protection of a decided behaviour. This is a spec-text ambiguity for the J-7 human-ruling list, not a measurable coverage cell.
